Any prompt sent regarding a spec (in ./spec) — e.g. to subagents via Agent or Workflow — must inherently include the Piton fluency text retrieved by running `piton claude --print-prompt`.

**Why:** The user asked for it; the spec is written in Piton (.pi), and agents without that fluency primer misread the syntax.

**How to apply:** Before delegating spec-related work, run `piton claude --print-prompt` and embed its full output in the agent prompt (fetch it fresh rather than paraphrasing). Related: ./spec is read-only, code lives in ./src.

content.content:
commitNote:
        Once a Code, Chain, or Spec task finishes without error, it adds a
        commit note summarising what it changed to the @{GitPanelScope}.

    history:
        Every task sent is saved in the project's `.suspense/history` directory
        as its hidden anchor's source, named by the second it was sent and the
        anchor's name. Once its run is over, what came of it is saved beside it
        in a `.json` file of the same name: the compiled userPrompt the harness
        received, each line the harness printed, and any error. Opening the
        project brings back every task in order, with its output replayed from
        that record. A task with no record shows as "Not recorded".

        Every question asked from the Ask tab is logged the same way, but in
        the project's `.suspense/asks` directory instead, so it never comes back
        as a task: its hidden anchor's source, and beside it a `.json` record
        of what came of it. The record is saved when the run is over, and also
        when the question is closed or replaced while it runs, with as much as
        the harness had done. A question that fails before it reaches the
        harness is logged too, with the error in its record.

    chatInput: @{ChatInputScope}

content.text:
Send this from the **Spec** tab to shape the concept first. Use **Chain** if you want it built in the same run.

```
The prompt history in @{PromptEditor} saves each task's whole harness output
("each line the harness printed"), which makes the history far larger than
anything the application reads back. Change what a run's `.json` record holds
to only what is needed to bring the task back as it was.

A record keeps, in the order they happened:
- the compiled userPrompt the harness received
- the conversation the run belonged to, so @{HarnessIntegrationScope} can
  carry on the latest conversation when the project is opened
- each piece of reply text, whole rather than as it streamed in
- each tool call: its name, the short summary of its input shown in the
  @{MessageList}, and whether it finished or failed
- the harness's final result, and whether it ended in error
- any error from outside the harness

It leaves out everything else the harness streams: partial text as it
arrives, tool results and file contents, full assistant messages, and
anything from subagents. The harness keeps its own full transcript of each
conversation, so none of that is lost to it.

A task or question brought back from its record looks and behaves exactly as
it did when it finished: the same output table rows, the same collapsed
answer steps for questions, the same status, and "Not recorded" when there is
no record. Questions in `.suspense/asks` are recorded the same way, including
a question closed or replaced while it runs.

Records already saved in the old form are rewritten in the new form the first
time the project is opened, keeping what they show, and are read correctly in
either form until then.
```

What the prompt settles:
- **Where it lands:** it points at the three scopes involved. The `history` section of `PromptEditor` (`spec/scope/prompt-mode/index.pi:114`) is the one that changes. `HarnessIntegrationScope` depends on the saved conversation id, and `MessageList` defines what replay has to reproduce.

The prompt history in @{PromptEditor} saves each task's whole harness output
("each line the harness printed"), which makes the history far larger than
anything the application reads back. Change what a run's `.json` record holds
to only what is needed to bring the task back as it was.

A record keeps, in the order they happened:
- the compiled userPrompt the harness received
- the conversation the run belonged to, so @{HarnessIntegrationScope} can
  carry on the latest conversation when the project is opened
- each piece of reply text, whole rather than as it streamed in
- each tool call: its name, the short summary of its input shown in the
  @{MessageList}, and whether it finished or failed
- the harness's final result, and whether it ended in error
- any error from outside the harness

It leaves out everything else the harness streams: partial text as it
arrives, tool results and file contents, full assistant messages, and
anything from subagents. The harness keeps its own full transcript of each
conversation, so none of that is lost to it.

A task or question brought back from its record looks and behaves exactly as
it did when it finished: the same output table rows, the same collapsed
answer steps for questions, the same status, and "Not recorded" when there is
no record. Questions in `.suspense/asks` are recorded the same way, including
a question closed or replaced while it runs.

Records already saved in the old form are rewritten in the new form the first
time the project is opened, keeping what they show, and are read correctly in
either form until then.
